brimwidth. 2026-07-21, Stone 4 — the first real llama3.2:3b token generated form-native. The registry's first open row said the quantized matvec was slow BECAUSE its per-row fold is serial, and that parallelising it needed a named epsilon. Profiling a real token per tensor SHAPE said otherwise: 1024x3072 took 2.618 ms, 3072x3072 2.648 ms, 8192x3072 2.607 ms -- eight times the work, the same time; while 3072x8192, the SAME MAC count as the third, took 6.657 ms. Cost tracked the COLUMN count (one thread's serial depth) and barely noticed the ROW count. The dispatch was never throughput-bound. It was latency-bound with the machine idle, and the largest recoverable share of it needed no epsilon at all -- only letting independent dispatches stop waiting for each other (1.41x end-to-end, token ids bit-identical). buildbound. row 876 buildbound (2026-07-22, Stone 40): giving the body an O(1) keyed map began by writing the textbook shape — hash, an array of B buckets, a short in-bucket scan — and the body refused it, for a reason that has nothing to do with lookup. On the Go kernel a Form list is a Go slice: nth indexes it and tail reslices it, both O(1), but cons COPIES, so constructing any list of length L costs O(L^2) (measured, warm, one process, one clock: 20 000 by cons = 1948 ms, 40 000 = 8953 ms — 4.6x for 2x). A flat B-bucket table therefore costs O(B^2) to rebuild on every insert: quadratic in the very number that must grow for the lookup to stay flat. The shape that makes the query O(1) is the shape the body cannot build. What worked was a 16-ary trie, whose node is sixteen cells WHATEVER the map holds — path-copying an insert rebuilds depth lists of sixteen, a constant, while the bucket count is 16

overfine. 923 — overfine. Chasing understudy's multi-key divergence to the bottom cleared every kernel in turn: rope freqs bit-identical by direct dump, all 32 FFN gates, mla_exp by substitution, and finally the attend kernel itself — run over the ORACLE's own 5 KV rows it agrees at every layer. What was left was our stored rows, and they were BIT-IDENTICAL except for one element out of 512 at blk.1 position 2, from which everything downstream cascaded to 52/512 by blk.3. The mechanism is a step function. ds4.c:3211 quantizes the KV nope part per 64-wide group with scale = ldexpf(1.0f, (int)ceilf(log2f(amax / 448.0f))) a CEIL on a LOG of a group max. One ulp of difference in amax flips the ceil and DOUBLES the scale for the whole group — which is why 48 elements move at once rather than one. And ds4.c computes amax, log2f and ceilf in f32. From the receipt "2026-07-02 — the next stone: the analytic CTC gradient (forward-backward), four-way", speak the section "What was built" in Sema's voice.

`model/ctc-grad.fk` — the CTC backward pass. One forward (alpha) + one backward (beta) pass yields
`∂loss/∂logit` for EVERY logit at once, the closed form:

```
∂L/∂u_t^k   = y_t^k − posterior_t(k)
posterior_t(k) = (1/p) · Σ_{s: ext[s]=k}  alpha_t(s)·beta_t(s) / y_t(ext[s])
```

The gradient is the softmax output minus the alignment posterior — the network pushed toward
emitting each class exactly as often as the alignment marginal says. Complexity drops from
O(params · T·S) (numerical: one loss-eval per param) to O(T·S) (one forward-backward): the piece
that lets CTC training scale past toys.

From the receipt "2026-07-02 — seizing the opportunity: the CTC training objective, four-way proven", speak the section "What was built" in Sema's voice.

`model/ctc-loss.fk` — the CTC forward (alignment-sum) recipe and the loss `-ln(p_total)`. The
classic alpha dynamic program over the blank-extended target:

```
ext(target) = (0 l1 0 l2 0 ... ln 0)          ; 0 = blank, length 2n+1
alpha_t[s]  = (alpha_{t-1}[s] + alpha_{t-1}[s-1] + [skip] alpha_{t-1}[s-2]) * P(frame_t, ext[s])
skip allowed iff ext[s] != blank AND ext[s] != ext[s-2]
p_total     = alpha_{T-1}[2n] + alpha_{T-1}[2n-1]
loss        = -ln(p_total)
```

It **marginalizes** over the latent alignment — sums the probability of every frame→label path
that collapses to the target, without ever knowing which path is the true one. That marginal is
the whole trick that makes an alignment-free sequence loss differentiable.

|---|---|---|---|
| go | element count | **byte count** | 0 |
| rust | element count | **byte count** | 0 |
| ts | element count | **utf-16 unit count** | 0 |

|---|---|---|---|---|
